key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn interpretable corrections to a simple k-ε-b turbulence closure, improving Rayleigh-Taylor mixing predictions during the transition to turbulence.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a way to upgrade RANS turbulence models for transitional mixing problems where standard closures are unreliable, without sacrificing model interpretability.
method: Embed the k-ε-b model inside a surrogate PINN.
Use the PINN to calibrate closure coefficients and identify missing-physics correction terms.
Rewrite the learned corrections as explicit analytical modifications using state variables and flow indicators.
evidence_signal: The corrected model is evaluated against an extensive DNS database of Rayleigh-Taylor flows and reported to improve mixing-layer growth predictions in the transitional regime.
watch_item: The learned closure is tailored to Rayleigh-Taylor transition data, so transferability to other flow regimes or geometries may require additional validation.
paper_title: Learning Turbulence Closures with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Rayleigh-Taylor Transition to Turbulence
